teaching_note.en: These are different Korean words with different spellings: 개 has ㅐ, while 게 has ㅔ.
teaching_note.ko: 개는 ㅐ를 쓰고, 게는 ㅔ를 써요.

verification.scope: Meaning supplied as new curriculum content; not confirmed from the existing curriculum.json arrays.
verification.notes: Standard dictionary entries identify 개 as 'dog' and 게 as 'crab.' Some modern Seoul speakers pronounce ㅐ and ㅔ very similarly or identically, so this contrast should emphasize spelling and word meaning rather than promise a consistently audible difference for every learner/speaker.

items.example_en: I drew a line on the paper.

teaching_note.en: 손 (hand) and 선 (line) differ only in the vowel: ㅓ vs ㅗ. Both are ordinary, everyday nouns.
teaching_note.ko: 손과 선은 모음만 달라요: ㅓ와 ㅗ.

verification.scope: Meaning supplied as new curriculum content; not confirmed from the existing curriculum.json arrays.
verification.notes: 손 verified as an elementary-level noun meaning 'hand' (body part). 선 verified as a basic noun meaning 'line' (its most common, beginner-level sense); 선 is polysemous in Korean (also 'meeting to choose a marriage partner', 'goodness/virtue' as Sino-Korean 善, etc.) but 'line' is the primary sense appropriate for this level. Neither form requires a grammatical host, unlike a particle.

teaching_note.en: 더 (more) and 도 (also/too) are not the same kind of word. 더 is an adverb that can stand in front of a verb on its own. 도 is a particle that always attaches directly to a noun, with no space — it never appears alone.
teaching_note.ko: 더는 부사라서 동사 앞에 혼자 올 수 있어요. 도는 조사라서 명사에 붙여 써요 — 혼자서는 쓰이지 않아요.

verification.scope: Meaning and grammatical behavior supplied as new curriculum content; not confirmed from the existing curriculum.json arrays.
verification.notes: 더 (more) verified as a basic adverb usable standalone before a verb (e.g. 더 주세요). 도 (also/too) verified as a case-marking-position particle that attaches directly to a noun with no space and cannot occur as a free-standing word — this is why the pair is classified lexical_vs_grammar_form rather than lexical_minimal_pair, and why both items are marked requires_host: true. Decodable from lesson 2 onward (ㄷ+ㅓ and ㄷ+ㅗ), earlier than either existing seed pair.
